questions.question_text: In which of the following groups are cells performing the same function arranged into tissues, without tissues being grouped into organs (tissue level of organisation)?

solution.explanation: NCERT: in sponges the cells are loose aggregates (cellular level). In coelenterates the arrangement is more complex: cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues (tissue level). From Platyhelminthes onwards tissues are grouped into organs (organ level), and in annelids, arthropods, molluscs, echinoderms and chordates organs associate to form organ systems (organ-system level).
solution.why_others_wrong: Porifera stop at the cellular level; flatworms form organs; annelids form organ systems.

solution.final_answer: Option C: Coelenterata

questions.question_text:

Notochord replaced by vertebral column in adult vertebrates → R true
